audits.title: LBSUN205 Clinical Practice Guidelines With Education Make A Difference

cycle1.result: Adherence to fluid management 66%, fixed rate insulin infusion 69% (later stated as 88%); average resolution time 27 hours.

cycle2.result: Fluid management 95%; fixed rate insulin 100%; resolution time 12.9 hours.

audits.other_findings: No mortality or serious complications reported.
audits.citation: . LBSUN205 Clinical Practice Guidelines With Education Make A Difference. J Endocr Soc. 2022;6(Suppl 1):A283-A284.

audits.title: Regular and frequent feedback of specific clinical criteria delivers a sustained improvement in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis .
audits.standard: Five specific targets: fluid prescription, fixed rate intravenous insulin infusion, glucose measurement, ketone measurement and specialist referral
audits.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (emergency medicine, acute medicine and diabetes departments)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit; mean average duration of DKA 22.0 hours.

audits.intervention: Quality improvement using PDSA cycles, with interventions including monthly feedback of specific clinical criteria to emergency medicine, acute medicine and diabetes departments.

cycle2.result: Mean average duration of DKA reduced to 10.2 hours.

audits.other_findings: Regular audit cycles were reported to give sustained improvement.
audits.citation: Kempegowda P, Coombs B, Nightingale P, Chandan JS, Al-Sheikhli J, Shyamanur B, et al.. Regular and frequent feedback of specific clinical criteria delivers a sustained improvement in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis . Clin Med (Lond). 2017;17(5):389-394. doi:10.7861/clinmedicine.17-5-389. PMID: 28974584.

audits.title: A Re-audit of the Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): The Importance of the Seven-Day Working Inpatient Diabetes Specialist Nurse Service.
audits.standard: Joint British Diabetes Societies DKA guidelines (18 standards)

cycle1.result: Previous audit (results not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Education, updated local guidelines and seven-day inpatient diabetes specialist nurse service.

cycle2.result: Improvement in 11 of 18 standards; 124 (98.4%) reviewed by diabetes specialist nurse.

audits.other_findings: Iatrogenic hypoglycaemia in 13 (10.3%) and transient hypokalaemia in 40 (31.7%).
audits.citation: Periyasami RK, Lim APW, Jayatilake DC, Oyibo SO. A Re-audit of the Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): The Importance of the Seven-Day Working Inpatient Diabetes Specialist Nurse Service. Cureus. 2024;16(3):e56723. doi:10.7759/cureus.56723. PMID: 38523875.

audits.title: Safety Audits in the Emergency Department: Applying the Threat and Error Model to the Management of Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
audits.setting: Paediatric emergency department, McMaster Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: 146 threats affected 43 (93%) visits; no visit error-free; communication errors and protocol non-adherence the commonest errors; unintended patient states in 30 (65%).

audits.citation: Tenedero CB, Soliman A, Samaan MC, Kam AJ. Safety Audits in the Emergency Department: Applying the Threat and Error Model to the Management of Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis. Pediatr Emerg Care. 2021;37(12):e1637-e1641. doi:10.1097/pec.0000000000002142. PMID: 32530837.

audits.title: A 10-year audit of pregnancies affected by diabetic ketoacidosis at the Pretoria Academic Complex.
audits.standard: Society for Endocrinology, Metabolism and Diabetes of South Africa DKA guidelines (intravenous fluids, insulin therapy, electrolyte management)

cycle1.result: Lack of adherence to the three cornerstones of therapy (fluids, insulin, electrolytes).

audits.other_findings: Of 49 (85.7%) women with recorded perinatal outcomes, 30.6% had stillbirths; 36 (64.3%) had type 1 diabetes.
audits.citation: Maseko NF, van Zyl D, Adam S. A 10-year audit of pregnancies affected by diabetic ketoacidosis at the Pretoria Academic Complex. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2022;158(3):557-563. doi:10.1002/ijgo.14093. PMID: 34997592.
